summary.en: Pakistan has halted trade at the Zangali and Torkham Iran crossings, creating a truck backlog, while limited trade has resumed under partial operations. Pakistan accuses the Taliban of using Afghan territory to launch attacks against it and rejects Taliban claims that Pakistani strikes have caused civilian casualties. The Taliban government has reshuffled civilian and military officials in Badakhshan, and Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have met with Iran amid renewed Houthi strikes. 1,794 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistan har stoppet handelen ved grenseovergangene Zangali og Torkham mot Iran, noe som har skapt en kø av lastebiler, mens begrenset handel har gjenopptatt under delvise operasjoner. Pakistan anklager Taliban for å bruke afghansk territorium til å starte angrep mot landet og avviser Talibans påstander om at pakistanske angrep har forårsaket sivile tap. Taliban-regjeringen har omorganisert sivile og militære tjenestemenn i Badakhshan, og Saudi-Arabia, Tyrkia og Pakistan har møtt Iran i kjølvannet av nye houthi-angrep. 1 794 dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
